title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages of this part of the 'équation des lacets' notes. SG is a group of SL2 type. G is the ambient group of GL2 type. R_{ρ,σ} is a group with a canonical character κ: R_{ρ,σ} → G_m. M̃_{ρ,σ} = R_{ρ,σ} × SG, and M_{ρ,σ} = M̃_{ρ,σ}/μ2 (diagonal). The homomorphism Θ: M̃ → G is given by Θ(r,u0) = κ(r)u0, whose determinant is κ(r)^2.

On the previous page Grothendieck fixed a torus i_{T0}: G_m ≅ T0 ⊂ G. He cut out M_{ρ,σ}(0) as the locus where Θ lands in the torus. This forces u0 = κ(r)^{-1} i_{T0}(κ(r)^2), i.e. a section/homomorphism φ0°: R_{ρ,σ} → SG (formula 13), which is the identity on μ2.

This page:
- He first remarks that for these preliminary computations one may take an arbitrary torus T0 (of a Borel) in SG and define (13).
- He then enlarges M(0), of dimension 3, to a 4-dimensional group M_{ρ,σ}[0] := Θ^{-1}(B'_0) (14). Here B'_0 = T0·L0 is the Borel subgroup, the semidirect product of the torus and its unipotent radical L0 (15).
- Now the element U = u0·κ(r) ∈ B'_0 is no longer determined by its determinant alone. The determinant fixes it only up to the unipotent part (written 'modulo κ(r)^2 … L0').
- The fibre over the SG factor is M[0] ∩ SG = B'_0 ∩ SG. From this L0 appears as a normal subgroup of M[0].
- Since M(0) ⊂ M[0] and M(0) ≅ T_{ρ,σ} (the torus-type group), one gets the semidirect decomposition M[0] = M(0)·L0 (16).
- So the data are: a torus T0 (as a 'picture', without fixing one) and a T0-stable subgroup L0 of SG.

On the next page this feeds into SM_{ρ,σ} = M[0]⋉SG, which contains M_{ρ,σ} = M(0)·SG. Grothendieck there admits he is losing the 'geometric' meaning. Overall this is elementary bookkeeping: passing from the torus to the Borel preimage under an isogeny-type map.
errors: No substantive mathematical error visible. The page is exploratory, and the next page records Grothendieck's own confusion about the geometric meaning of the construction.
The statement 'determines U only modulo κ(r)^2' is loosely phrased. What is meant is that the determinant fixes only the toral component, and U is undetermined up to the unipotent L0-part.

ideas.what: Replace the torus-preimage M(0) = Θ^{-1}(T0) by the Borel-preimage M[0] = Θ^{-1}(T0·L0). This gives a semidirect product decomposition M[0] = M(0)⋉L0 with L0 the unipotent radical.
ideas.modern_name: Preimage of a Borel subgroup under an isogeny/central extension; Levi decomposition B = T⋉U

ideas.what: A section φ0°: R → SG built from a character κ and a cocharacter i_{T0}, restricting to the identity on μ2.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of a μ2-central quotient via a torus

deep.surprise_reason: Routine algebraic-group bookkeeping (Borel preimage, Levi decomposition) inside a larger exploratory computation. There is no new result or connection on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: 'U = U_0 K(σ)' and 'modulo K(σ)^2' should read κ(r) (the character κ applied to r), consistent with the previous page: 'U = u_0 κ(r)', 'modulo κ(r)^2'.
The intersection written as '𝒢^+_{ρ,σ}' appears with SG written above it. The intended statement is M_{ρ,σ}[0] ∩ SG = B'_0 ∩ SG.
'n'est pas déterminé par la seule connaissance du 2-déterminant' more likely reads 'de son déterminant'.
